subtopics.title: Cyclic Quadrilaterals — Opposite Angles Add to One Eighty

questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, angle A = 105°. Angle C is:
options: 75° — opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary

questions.question: The proof that opposite angles are supplementary works because their two central angles:
options: Together sweep the full 360° about the centre

questions.question: The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals:
options: Half the reflex angle at the centre

questions.question: The supplementary-opposite-angles theorem may be quoted only when:
options: The quadrilateral has a pair of parallel sides
All four vertices genuinely lie on the circle, in cyclic order

questions.question: To prove a quadrilateral cyclic using opposite angles, you need:
options: One pair supplementary — the other pair then follows automatically

questions.question: The third converse test says four points share a circle when a segment subtends:
options: A right angle at each of the two points
Supplementary angles at two points on the same side
Equal angles at two points on the same side of the segment
Equal angles at two points on opposite sides

questions.question: Given a produced (extended) side of a quadrilateral, the natural cyclic test is:
options: Exterior angle equals interior opposite angle
Equal angles on the same base

questions.question: Proving a quadrilateral cyclic matters in long riders because:
options: It doubles the marks for the diagram
It replaces the need for reasons
It proves the quadrilateral is also a parallelogram
It unlocks the whole circle toolbox for those four points in later parts

subtopics.title: Tangents — the Perpendicular Radius and the Two Equal Tangents

questions.question: The tangent to a circle and the radius drawn to the point of contact meet at:
options: 90° — quoted as tangent perpendicular to radius
The angle in the alternate segment

questions.question: P is 17 units from the centre of a circle of radius 8. The tangent from P has length:
The two tangents drawn from the same external point are:
options: Equal in length — proved by RHS congruency

questions.question: Tangents from P touch at A and B with angle APB = 52°. Angles PAB and PBA are each:
options: 64° — isosceles triangle, then the angle sum

subtopics.title: The Tangent-Chord Theorem and a Full Rider

questions.question: The angle between a tangent and a chord at the point of contact equals:
options: The angle subtended by that chord in the alternate segment
The angle at the centre on the same arc
Half the angle in the same segment
90° minus the angle at the centre

questions.question: Tangent at A, chord AB, tangent-chord angle 58°. Any angle on AB from the alternate segment is:
In the full rider with angle APB = 52°, angle ACB on the major arc came out as:
options: 64° — via the isosceles base angles and tangent-chord

questions.question: The independent cross-check used quadrilateral OAPB by computing:
options: 360° − 90° − 90° − 52° = 128° at the centre, then halving to 64°
The sum of the two tangent lengths

subtopics.title: Two Arcs That Share the Whole Circle

questions.question: The angles at opposite posts B and D stand on two arcs that together make:
options: The entire circle — nothing missed, nothing counted twice

questions.question: The centre's two claims — double B and double D — must total:
Walking out through gate C, the angle outside the kraal equals the angle at A because:
options: Both complete the interior angle at C to a straight 180°

subtopics.title: The Kerb and the Two Ropes

questions.question: The spoke from the hub to where the wheel touches the kerb is:
options: Perfectly square to the kerb — at every point of contact

questions.question: Standing 17 paces from the hub of a tank of radius 8, the rope touching the side measures:
options: 15 paces — Pythagoras on the guaranteed right angle

questions.question: Two ropes from one peg to a circular kraal wall are equal because:
options: The peg is on the wall
The line from peg to centre is a mirror — each rope reflects onto the other

questions.question: Ropes opening at 52° at the peg give base angles at the wall of:
In the echo picture, the tangent-chord angle echoes to:
options: The alternate segment — the arc on the far side of the chord
The same side of the chord

questions.question: A tangent-chord angle of 58° means the angle 180° − 58° = 122° echoes to:
options: The other arc — each side of the chord serves its own audience

questions.question: The echo only works when the chord is drawn from:
options: The exact point where the tangent touches the circle

questions.question: In the story rider — ropes at 52° — the listener on the major arc catches:
options: 64°, confirmed by the greedy-centre road: half of 128°
